signal: Seso raised a $26M Series B led by BOND to expand its ag workforce platform with AI-enabled payroll, banking, and HR tooling for farm employers

email.body1:
Matthew, saw Seso raise its $26M Series B to expand AI payroll and HR for ag employers.

Scaling the platform that fast usually means more in-market accounts than the team can cover before reps ramp, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Seso off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing those tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Matthew, quick follow-up for Seso.

Post-raise, the pipeline number usually climbs faster than headcount can. Most teams can't say how many meetings they need to book to hit the new target, so the gap shows up late and recovering the quarter gets expensive.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Seso needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Matthew, last bit of proof for Seso.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Seso's reply rate likely compares to other Series-B startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Matthew, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. The post-raise stretch is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I'll tailor it to Seso either way.
